Britain’s Prime Minister Keir Starmer talks with Shanghai Party Secretary Chen Jining during a bilateral meeting in Shanghai, China, on Saturday, January 31, 2026 [Kin Cheung/AP]

articles.title: Families blame Witkoff for withholding key designation from Americans jailed in Russia
articles.summary: Some families of Americans jailed in Russia are raising concerns that the Trump administration is holding back a key tool to advocate for their loved ones’ release, and are pointing the blame directly at Steve Witkoff. Two family members, along with a Senate aide and advocacy group, see Trump’s special envoy as blocking the labeling…
articles.body:
Some families of Americans jailed in Russia are raising concerns that the Trump administration is holding back a key tool to advocate for their loved ones’ release, and are pointing the blame directly at Steve Witkoff.

Two family members, along with a Senate aide and advocacy group, see Trump’s special envoy as blocking the labeling of at least five Americans as “wrongfully detained,” a designation developed by Congress to elevate their cases to the highest levels of the U.S. government to push for their freedom.

“When I talk to the State Department, they basically tell me it’s all up to Witkoff,” said Harold Jezler, whose wife Olga has been jailed in Russia since June 2022.

A Senate aide said their office heard that Witkoff is holding back the “wrongfully detained” designation to avoid aggravating the Kremlin.

“The way they explain it is that they feel they don’t want to upset the Russians,” he said. “They feel it might raise the price in the negotiations. But on the other hand, the Russians don’t really know that we’re serious about these people until we designate them.”

President Trump embraced Russian President Vladimir Putin as his “friend” earlier this month, following a brief bilateral meeting and then trilateral summit alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The president has succeeded in bringing home at least two Americans from Russia who were labeled as “wrongfully detained”: Robert Gillman in August, and Stephen Hubbard in October.

Witkoff, who picked up Hubbard in Russia, was criticized for fawning over Putin on the trip, calling him a “humanitarian” for releasing the American.

A State Department spokesman said that Secretary of State Marco Rubio makes wrongful detention determinations.

“In every case when a U.S. national is detained overseas, including in Russia, the Department of State continuously reviews the circumstances surrounding the detention for indicators of wrongfulness,” the spokesman said.

“There are currently no Americans determined to be wrongfully detained in Russia. This Administration continues to work for the release of all Americans unjustly detained around the world.”

Robin Stultz is the sister of Chuck Zimmerman, a Navy veteran who was arrested by Russia in June 2025. He was arrested aboard his sailboat in the Black Sea — part of an around-the-world trip he was making — and charged with arms trafficking when he voluntarily declared the firearm he kept on board.

Stultz said the State Department has advised her in the past that labeling her brother “wrongfully detained” could make negotiations for his release “more difficult,” as the Russians could demand “a higher price for him”.

“I know Witkoff right now is the point person and we’ve pleaded to Marco Rubio numerous times. We know that President Trump’s mission has been, and he’s done very well with it over the last several years, of getting Americans home,” Stultz said.

“And we’re just not really understanding why anyone underneath him is not following through with his wishes. We’re not understanding why they haven’t been — being [designated] wrongfully detained and gotten out of there.”

In a letter to Rubio in October, Rep. Ben Cline (R-Va.) called for Zimmerman to be declared “wrongfully detained,” and raised concern about his deteriorating health.

Cline previously wrote to Rubio in June alongside Sens. Mark Warner (D-Va.) and Tim Kaine (D-Va.) advocating for Zimmerman.

In August, Warner and Kaine joined Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), along with 13 other Democratic senators, in a letter to Rubio calling for Zimmerman, Jezler, and three others to be designated as wrongfully detained, which would elevate their cases to the Special Envoy for Hostage Negotiations (SPEHA).

“This valuable tool would maximize U.S. government coordination and advance negotiations to ensure their swift release, and the designation is key for providing needed resources to the families as they advocate for their loved ones and heal and other support to released detainees upon their return to the U.S.,” the senators wrote in the letter.

The detainees also include Andre Khachatoorian, jailed since Dec. 2021; David Barnes, jailed since Jan 2022; and Alexsandr Antonov, jailed since March 2025.

The SPEHA was developed by Congress in the same law creating the “wrongfully detained” label, part of the Robert Levinson Act. The bill was included in the 2021 National Defense Authorization Act, which Congress passed over a veto issued by Trump.

Rubio, then a Florida senator, was a co-sponsor of the bill.

There are between 20 and 25 Americans jailed in Russia, although non-government groups aren’t able to properly assess if they all meet the criteria for “wrongful detention”.

Eric Lebson is an advocate for the five Americans singled out by lawmakers. He is chief strategy officer for Global Reach, a nonprofit organization dedicated to bringing home Americans who are wrongly held abroad.

He expressed frustration that Witkoff, alongside Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, had succeeded in negotiating a large-scale prisoner-of-war exchange between Russia and Ukraine in November but had not appeared to make progress on freeing the jailed Americans.

“Each of these people meets the criteria for designation. They need President Trump’s intervention,” Lebson said. “There are two rules here: one, when you’re designated, you come home. And two, when President Trump knows your name, you come home. Those are the two rules.”

The day before Hubbard was released from Russian detention, Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that he personally appealed to Putin for his freedom.

“I’ve been talking to President Putin about Mr. Hubbard. I’ve been talking to him at length. I’ve asked him to release him, let’s see what happens,” Trump said on Oct. 20 .

Trump added that his decision to waive congressionally mandated sanctions on Russia was done to preserve negotiations for Hubbard’s release .

ABC News reported at the time that Witkoff was negotiating for Hubbard and “multiple Americans” to be released from detention in Russia.

“We assess bilateral concerns are impacting designation decisions,” said Elizabeth Richards, director of hostage advocacy and research with the James W. Foley Legacy Foundation.

The Foley Foundation advocates for American hostages and wrongful detainees held abroad and promotes journalist safety — regardless of whatever bilateral tensions surround the case.

An administration can also keep a designation private, which they have done before.

Richards said she has heard similar stories along the lines of Witkoff holding back “wrongful detention” designations to preserve ties with Russia.

The White House did not address a question from The Hill on whether Trump raised the cases of Americans jailed in Russia when he met with Putin in China last week.

“President Trump cares deeply about the return of Americans detained abroad, which is why he has brought home over 100 Americans from around the world,” a White House official responded.

Stultz said she was “let down” and hurt, under the impression that her brother’s case wasn’t raised because she’s heard nothing from the U.S. government. She spoke with The Hill the day before Zimmerman’s youngest daughter’s birthday, calling it a “tough day.” Stultz received a screenshot of a birthday card Zimmerman made for his daughter.

“This is the second birthday he’s missed. She’s getting ready to finish elementary school and start middle school. He’s missing out on a lot,” she said.

Jezler said he’s frustrated over what appears to be Trump failing to put Americans first and instead appeasing Putin as a way to end the war in Ukraine. He listed off the waiving of sanctions, Trump’s decision to purchase Russian diesel, facilitating the prisoner of war exchange, and choking off U.S. support for Kyiv.

“He ran on America First, and we need to prioritize bringing home the Americans,” he said.
